Chapter 1 Introduction

This webbook provides all the code used in the analyses for the study “Micro-scale spatial metagenomics: revealing high-resolution spatial biogeography of gut microbiomes”. The project 3D’omics (http://www.3domics.eu) was Funded by European Union’s Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation programme.

1.1 Prepare the R environment

1.1.1 Environment

To reproduce all the analyses locally, clone this repository in your computer using:

RStudio > New Project > Version Control > Git

And indicating the following git repository:

https://github.com/3d-omics/MSSM.git

Once the R project has been created, follow the instructions and code chunks shown in this webbook.

1.1.2 Libraries

The following R packages are required for the data analysis. Most modules can be installed directly from CRAN or GitHub. However, four modules are provided through Bioconductor and should be installed if needed with the command below before loading:

# install.packages('BiocManager', dependencies = TRUE)
# BiocManager::install(c("phyloseq", "ggtreeExtra","ggtree", "ALDEx2"))'

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
# If the package is not installed, installs from CRAN
pacman::p_load(
  tidyverse, rairtable, jsonlite, ape,
  ggpubr, broom, reshape2, zCompositions, ANCOMBC,
  ALDEx2, car, DHARMa, sjPlot, ggeffects,
  ggh4x, vegan, ggfortify, ggrepel, microbiome, ggforce, patchwork,
  grid, pheatmap, janitor, spdep, adespatial, adegraphics,
  ade4, magick, permuco, airtabler2, rmarkdown, purrr, PerformanceAnalytics
)
# If the package is not installed, installs from GitHub
pacman::p_load_gh(
  "anttonalberdi/hilldiv2",
  "anttonalberdi/distillR",
  "wilkelab/cowplot",
  "david-barnett/microViz"
)
select <- dplyr::select
recode <- dplyr::recode
